slides.texte_overlay:
small signals that someone
wants more of your time

they ask follow up questions

they don't just nod, they ask more about what you said. wanting to know more is one of the clearest signs someone enjoys your company. it sounds simple, but very few people actually do it.

they reply with questions

their messages end with a question, so the conversation keeps going. people who want to keep talking always leave the door open for your reply. over time, it quietly changes how you feel every day.

they share their plans

they mention where they'll be this weekend, almost as an invitation. letting you know their plans is often a quiet, hopeful way of saying they'd love you to join.

they love your stories

people want more time with someone who always has something surprising to tell. the more you practise it, the more natural it becomes. it's a small change with a surprisingly big effect.
slides.texte_sophia:
they love your stories

people always want more of my stories now. the Sophia app turns learning into one short lesson a day, a strange myth or a fact, and every conversation runs longer.

slides.texte_overlay:
they remember small things

they bring up a tiny detail you mentioned weeks ago. we only remember small things about people we pay close attention to, without even trying. try it for one week and notice the difference.
